commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1948203 - Skip alt-svc validation if we already connected to the server, r=necko-reviewers,jesup

This patch optimizes how Firefox handles speculative connections for alt-svc headers. When a server sends an alt-svc header, Firefox normally creates a speculative connection to validate it. With this patch, if the connection’s hash key matches the one generated from the alt-svc header, the validation step is skipped since an equivalent connection is already in place, avoiding unnecessary work.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D238218
pr_title: Use conn info from TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo in TRRServiceChannel
pr_description:
In `TRRServiceChannel::OnStartRequest()`, obtain the connection info atomically via `TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo()` rather than calling `TakeResponseHead()` for the response head and then `GetConnInfo()` separately for the connection info.

`TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo()` acquires the appropriate mutex lock before reading the connection info, ensuring the object is not concurrently modified or freed by other threads while we access it. The returned `connInfo` is then passed directly to `ProcessAltService()`, eliminating the need for the separate unprotected `GetConnInfo()` call.

This brings `TRRServiceChannel` in line with the pattern already used in `nsHttpChannel`, which has always retrieved both the response head and connection info together under the lock.

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1970764 - Use conn info from TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo, r=necko-reviewers,valentin

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D252804
agent_reasoning: The buggy code called `mTransaction->TakeResponseHead()` to get the response head and then separately called `mTransaction->GetConnInfo()` to retrieve the connection info for passing to `ProcessAltService()`. `GetConnInfo()` accesses `mConnInfo` without holding any mutex, while other threads can concurrently modify or free that object, creating a data race (use-after-free) that could crash the browser. The fix uses `TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo()` instead of `TakeResponseHead()`, which retrieves both the response head and a ref-counted snapshot of the connection info under the appropriate lock in a single atomic call. The resulting `connInfo` RefPtr is then passed directly to `ProcessAltService()`, removing the racy `GetConnInfo()` call entirely.
